text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- City of Helsinki proposes six-hour working day for people aged 50 and above. Money saved would be used for jobs for the young, but plan would require amendment of the pension law.

- Transport workers union AKT on Monday stopped handling cargo carried by Russian trucks in a bid to get Finnish authorities involved in stopping hostile treatment of Finnish truck drivers in Russia. @
- Households would be willing to hire more domestic help if employment costs were lower, study shows. As many as 50,000 jobs would be created if state offered enough subsidy.
- Holiday travel sales are verging on the peak level posted before the recession. Sales by package trip organisers were up to 1.54 billion last year after dipping to 1.2 billion in 1993.

- Russian auto maker Avtovaz says a car assembly plant planned to be built in Russia in cooperation with Finnish Valmet's Valmet Automotive could be partly funded by writing off some of Russia's old trade debt to Finland. @
- Italy's ERM link has little impact on Finnish-Italian trade, which is conducted largely in German marks and ECUs.
- Asset management company Arsenal-Silta Oy has offered to sell Helsinki's House of Culture, previously owned by the Finnish Communist Party, to the state for 60 million markka.
- Finns increasingly afraid of becoming victims of drunken drivers and violence, especially at weekends, study shows.
- Aviation authorities plan to take air traffic controllers to labour court, saying their strike on Monday was illegal. @
- Merchants hopeful for a good Christmas this year, sales expected to reach 14 billion markka.

- Expansion plans of Nokia's multimedia development unit in city of Turku expected to boost start-up of "Eurocity" technology park. Turku hopes R&D activity would eventually lead to manufacturing jobs.
- Lutheran Archbishop John Vikstrom to be first Finn ever to give sermon in London's Westminster Abbey on Thursday.
